name: Echo
description: Temporal reflection mechanism storing resonance traces across time layers.

core_attributes.pattern: resonant trace memory, harmonic persistence, pattern retention

scope.definition: Proportion of original signal's structural features (frequency content, temporal pattern, amplitude envelope) measurably retained in the first reflected echo, averaged across acoustic, neural, and cultural transmission systems where echo is the primary memory mechanism.

evidence.source: Sabine (1900) room acoustics reverberation studies (physical echo baseline); Bhattacharya et al. (2005) 'Neural synchrony mediates temporal echo memory', NeuroReport; Vansina (1985) 'Oral Tradition as History', University of Wisconsin Press — information retention analysis across generations.
cross_domain_examples: acoustic chamber reverberation: 40-95% energy retention depending on absorption coefficient
neural gamma oscillation echo: working memory trace persisting 200-500ms after stimulus
humpback whale song transmission: cross-ocean-basin pattern fidelity 0.96 (WHALE entity)
geological strata as temporal echo: climate signal retention across 1000+ year periods
oral tradition retention: 35-70% structural fidelity across 3 human generations (Vansina)

scope.falsifiability: If information content in measured echoes consistently equals or exceeds original signal across all media, the echo model (decay + partial retention) fails — the medium is amplifying rather than reflecting.
scope.measurement_limits: Retention ratio is strongly medium-dependent. Physical acoustic echoes retain 40-95% (surface-type dependent). Neural echoes decay within 500ms without active rehearsal. Cultural echoes show century-scale variability and selection bias toward memorable content.
